name: SSC Direct and Indirect Speech
description: Narration transformations covering statements, questions, commands, requests, exclamations, and tense changes.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am tired after the meeting."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was tired after the meeting.

Rule: When the reporting verb is in the past, present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Past reporting verb pulls the tense one step back, so am becomes was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I like this book."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she liked that book.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple, and this usually changes to that.

Memory hook: In indirect speech, the speaker’s “this book” becomes the reporter’s “that book.”

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: Ravi said, "I know the answer."
cards.definition:
Indirect: Ravi said that he knew the answer.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Know becomes knew, but confidence still needs proof.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "You are late."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher told him that he was late.

Rule: Said to becomes told, and pronouns change according to meaning.

Memory hook: You changes according to the person being spoken to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "You are honest."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told me that I was honest.

Rule: Said to changes to told, and you becomes I because the listener is me.

Memory hook: Pronouns follow the speaker-listener relationship, not the original words blindly.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "You are careless."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told him that he was careless.

Rule: Said to becomes told, and you becomes he.

Memory hook: The quoted “you” points to him, so it becomes he.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We are ready."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they were ready.

Rule: We changes according to the speaker, and are becomes were.

Memory hook: We follows the speakers, so they said they were ready.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: I said, "I am not afraid."
cards.definition:
Indirect: I said that I was not afraid.

Rule: I remains I when the same person reports, and am becomes was.

Memory hook: The pronoun may stay, but the tense still steps back.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "My brother is ill."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that his brother was ill.

Rule: My changes to his, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: My follows the original speaker, so it becomes his.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "My phone is missing."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that her phone was missing.

Rule: My changes to her, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: The phone changes owner in grammar, not in real life.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "Our plan is simple."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that their plan was simple.

Rule: Our changes to their, and present tense changes to past tense.

Memory hook: Our follows they, so it becomes their.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am writing a letter."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was writing a letter.

Rule: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

Memory hook: Am writing becomes was writing.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am cooking dinner."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she was cooking dinner.

Rule: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

Memory hook: The action continues, but the tense moves backward.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We are playing chess."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they were playing chess.

Rule: Are playing changes to were playing.

Memory hook: Are becomes were in reported speech with a past reporting verb.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The boy said, "I am flying a kite."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The boy said that he was flying a kite.

Rule: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

Memory hook: The kite stays in the sky, but grammar lands in the past.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "The baby is sleeping."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that the baby was sleeping.

Rule: Is sleeping changes to was sleeping.

Memory hook: Sleeping remains sleeping, only is becomes was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have finished my homework."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had finished his homework.

Rule: Present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Have finished becomes had finished.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I have seen this movie."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had seen that movie.

Rule: Have seen becomes had seen, and this becomes that.

Memory hook: Present perfect travels back to past perfect.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We have solved the puzzle."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had solved the puzzle.

Rule: Have solved changes to had solved.

Memory hook: Have becomes had, but the solved puzzle stays solved.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The clerk said, "I have sent the file."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The clerk said that he had sent the file.

Rule: Present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Has/have sent becomes had sent.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have been waiting since morning."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had been waiting since morning.

Rule: Present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Have been waiting becomes had been waiting.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I have been studying for three hours."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had been studying for three hours.

Rule: Present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: The duration remains, but have becomes had.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We have been working here since 2020."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had been working there since 2020.

Rule: Have been working changes to had been working, and here changes to there.

Memory hook: Here usually becomes there.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I went to Delhi yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had gone to Delhi the previous day.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect, and yesterday changes to the previous day.

Memory hook: Yesterday becomes the previous day in reported speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I met him last week."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had met him the previous week.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect, and last week changes to the previous week.

Memory hook: Last week becomes the previous week.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We bought a car last month."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had bought a car the previous month.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect, and last month changes to the previous month.

Memory hook: Bought becomes had bought.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I lost my pen."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had lost his pen.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Lost becomes had lost, though the pen is still missing.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The witness said, "I saw the thief."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The witness said that he had seen the thief.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Saw becomes had seen.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I was reading a novel."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had been reading a novel.

Rule: Past continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Was reading becomes had been reading.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I was repairing my bike."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had been repairing his bike.

Rule: Past continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Was repairing becomes had been repairing.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We were watching the match."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had been watching the match.

Rule: Past continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Were watching becomes had been watching.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The girl said, "I was waiting for the bus."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The girl said that she had been waiting for the bus.

Rule: Past continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Waiting stays, but was becomes had been.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I had already eaten."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had already eaten.

Rule: Past perfect usually remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Past perfect is already far back, so it does not step back again.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I had finished the work before noon."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had finished the work before noon.

Rule: Past perfect remains past perfect.

Memory hook: Had finished stays had finished.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We had never seen such rain."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had never seen such rain.

Rule: Past perfect generally remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Had never seen remains had never seen.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I will help you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he would help me.

Rule: Will changes to would, and you changes according to the listener.

Memory hook: Will becomes would in reported speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I shall return tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would return the next day.

Rule: Shall often changes to would, and tomorrow changes to the next day.

Memory hook: Tomorrow becomes the next day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The coach said, "We will win the match."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The coach said that they would win the match.

Rule: Will changes to would, and we changes to they.

Memory hook: Will is future in direct speech, would is its reported form.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I can lift this box."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he could lift that box.

Rule: Can changes to could, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Can becomes could.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I may join the class."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she might join the class.

Rule: May changes to might.

Memory hook: May becomes might, like certainty becoming weaker.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I must leave now."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had to leave then.

Rule: Must often changes to had to, and now changes to then.

Memory hook: Must becomes had to when it shows obligation.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The doctor said, "You must take rest."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The doctor told him that he had to take rest.

Rule: Must showing necessity changes to had to.

Memory hook: Medical advice in reported speech often becomes had to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "You should revise daily."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told me that I should revise daily.

Rule: Should usually remains should.

Memory hook: Should is already a modal of advice, so it usually stays.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I could solve it."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he could solve it.

Rule: Could generally remains could.

Memory hook: Could does not need another backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I would rather stay home."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would rather stay home.

Rule: Would usually remains would.

Memory hook: Would is already in past-form modal shape.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I might come late."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he might come late.

Rule: Might usually remains might.

Memory hook: Might stays might because it is already cautious.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.

Rule: Universal truths do not change tense.

Memory hook: Scientific truth does not backshift just because someone reported it.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Honesty is the best policy."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that honesty is the best policy.

Rule: Proverbs and universal truths usually remain unchanged.

Memory hook: A proverb stays timeless.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Water boils at 100°C."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.

Rule: Scientific facts remain in present tense.

Memory hook: Water does not change its boiling point for narration grammar.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Two and two make four."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that two and two make four.

Rule: Mathematical truths do not change tense.

Memory hook: Arithmetic refuses dramatic tense changes.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The guide said, "The Taj Mahal stands in Agra."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The guide said that the Taj Mahal stands in Agra.

Rule: Geographical or permanent facts may remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Permanent facts often keep present tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He says, "I am ready."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He says that he is ready.

Rule: If the reporting verb is present, the tense usually does not change.

Memory hook: Present reporting verb does not push the tense backward.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She says, "I like tea."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She says that she likes tea.

Rule: With says, tense remains the same.

Memory hook: Says keeps the original time zone.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They say, "We are innocent."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They say that they are innocent.

Rule: Present reporting verb means no backshift.

Memory hook: Say in present keeps are as are.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He will say, "I am busy."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He will say that he is busy.

Rule: Future reporting verb usually does not cause backshift.

Memory hook: Will say reports from the future but keeps the statement’s tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The notice says, "The office is closed."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The notice says that the office is closed.

Rule: Present reporting verb says keeps the tense unchanged.

Memory hook: Notices report facts directly, not emotionally.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am going now."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was going then.

Rule: Now changes to then, and present continuous changes to past continuous.

Memory hook: Now becomes then.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will come tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would come the next day.

Rule: Tomorrow changes to the next day.

Memory hook: Tomorrow becomes the next day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I met him yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had met him the previous day.

Rule: Yesterday changes to the previous day.

Memory hook: Yesterday steps back to the previous day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I bought this pen today."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had bought that pen that day.

Rule: Today changes to that day, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Today becomes that day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We will start tonight."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they would start that night.

Rule: Tonight changes to that night.

Memory hook: Tonight becomes that night.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I saw her last night."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had seen her the previous night.

Rule: Last night changes to the previous night.

Memory hook: Last night becomes the previous night.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will finish this work next week."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would finish that work the following week.

Rule: Next week changes to the following week.

Memory hook: Next becomes following.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I came here yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had gone there the previous day.

Rule: Come may change to go depending on reporting position, here changes to there.

Memory hook: Here becomes there, and came often becomes gone.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "This is my house."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that that was her house.

Rule: This changes to that, my changes to her, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: This becomes that in the reporter’s hands.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "These mangoes are sweet."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that those mangoes were sweet.

Rule: These changes to those, and are changes to were.

Memory hook: These becomes those.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am leaving now."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was leaving then.

Rule: Now changes to then.

Memory hook: Direct “now” is reported as “then.”

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will call you the day after tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would call me in two days' time.

Rule: The day after tomorrow changes to in two days' time.

Memory hook: Future time phrases are shifted from the reporting point.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I met him the day before yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had met him two days before.

Rule: The day before yesterday changes to two days before.

Memory hook: The reporter counts backward from the reporting time.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Are you ready?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I was ready.

Rule: Yes/no questions use asked + whether/if, statement order, and tense backshift.

Memory hook: The question mark disappears, and word order becomes normal.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Do you know the answer?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked him whether he knew the answer.

Rule: Do/does questions become whether/if clauses without do/does.

Memory hook: Do vanishes in indirect yes/no questions.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said to us, "Are you coming with us?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: They asked us whether we were going with them.

Rule: Question changes to statement order, are becomes were, and pronouns change.

Memory hook: Coming may become going depending on viewpoint.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to her, "Have you finished the work?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked her whether she had finished the work.

Rule: Present perfect in a question changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Have finished becomes had finished.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Did you see my bag?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me whether I had seen her bag.

Rule: Simple past question changes to past perfect in indirect speech.

Memory hook: Did you see becomes whether I had seen.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the boys, "Have you done your homework?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked the boys whether they had done their homework.

Rule: Have done changes to had done, and question order becomes statement order.

Memory hook: Homework questions sound scarier in indirect speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Can you lend me your pen?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I could lend him my pen.

Rule: Can changes to could, and pronouns change according to meaning.

Memory hook: Can you becomes whether I could.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Will you help me?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked him whether he would help her.

Rule: Will changes to would.

Memory hook: Will you help becomes whether he would help.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The officer said to the clerk, "Is the file ready?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The officer asked the clerk whether the file was ready.

Rule: Is changes to was and question order becomes statement order.

Memory hook: The file remains calm, the clerk does not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me where I lived.

Rule: Wh-questions keep the question word but use statement order and backshift.

Memory hook: Do you live becomes I lived.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "What are you doing?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked him what he was doing.

Rule: Present continuous question changes to past continuous statement order.

Memory hook: What are you doing becomes what he was doing.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said to me, "Why did you leave early?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: They asked me why I had left early.

Rule: Simple past question changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Why did you leave becomes why I had left.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to her, "When will you return?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked her when she would return.

Rule: Will changes to would and statement order is used.

Memory hook: When will you becomes when she would.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to Ravi, "How did you solve it?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked Ravi how he had solved it.

Rule: Did questions change to had + V3 when backshifted.

Memory hook: How did becomes how he had.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Which book do you want?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me which book I wanted.

Rule: Wh-question changes to statement order.

Memory hook: Do disappears, wanted appears.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to them, "Who is making noise?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked them who was making noise.

Rule: Who-question changes to indirect form with backshift.

Memory hook: Is making becomes was making.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The coach said to the player, "Why are you running slowly?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The coach asked the player why he was running slowly.

Rule: Are running changes to was running.

Memory hook: The running slows down, and so does the tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "How long have you been waiting?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me how long I had been waiting.

Rule: Present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

Memory hook: Have been waiting becomes had been waiting.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to her, "Where have you kept the keys?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked her where she had kept the keys.

Rule: Present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: The keys remain missing, but the tense becomes had kept.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the student, "Why have you not submitted the form?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked the student why he had not submitted the form.

Rule: Have not submitted changes to had not submitted.

Memory hook: Forms become serious when reported by teachers.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Do not waste time."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told him not to waste time.

Rule: Negative commands use told/ordered/advised + object + not to + V1.

Memory hook: Do not becomes not to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the boys, "Stand up."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher ordered the boys to stand up.

Rule: Commands use ordered/told + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: The command becomes to stand.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Please help me."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He requested me to help him.

Rule: Requests use requested + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Please often signals requested.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to her brother, "Please bring me a glass of water."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She requested her brother to bring her a glass of water.

Rule: Please changes the reporting verb to requested.

Memory hook: Polite commands become requests.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The officer said to the guard, "Open the gate."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The officer ordered the guard to open the gate.

Rule: Official commands often use ordered.

Memory hook: Open becomes to open.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The doctor said to the patient, "Take this medicine twice a day."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The doctor advised the patient to take that medicine twice a day.

Rule: Advice uses advised + object + to + V1, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Doctors usually advise, not merely say.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to me, "Revise the chapter again."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher advised me to revise the chapter again.

Rule: Advice or instruction can use advised/told + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Revise becomes to revise.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: Mother said to the child, "Do not touch the hot pan."
cards.definition:
Indirect: Mother warned the child not to touch the hot pan.

Rule: Warnings use warned + object + not to + V1.

Memory hook: Do not touch becomes not to touch.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The policeman said to the driver, "Show me your licence."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The policeman ordered the driver to show him his licence.

Rule: Commands use ordered + object + to + V1 and pronouns change.

Memory hook: Your follows the driver, so it becomes his.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Let us go for a walk."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He suggested to me that we should go for a walk.

Rule: Let us often changes to suggested that + subject + should.

Memory hook: Let us becomes suggested that we should.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Let us start the meeting."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She suggested that they should start the meeting.

Rule: Let us as proposal becomes suggested that they should.

Memory hook: Let us is not a command, it is a suggestion.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The captain said, "Let us try again."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The captain suggested that they should try again.

Rule: Let us changes to suggested that they should.

Memory hook: Team spirit becomes a suggestion.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to his friend, "Let me speak."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He requested his friend to let him speak.

Rule: Let me often becomes requested/asked + object + to let + pronoun + V1.

Memory hook: Let me stays close to allow me.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to the guard, "Let me enter."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She requested the guard to let her enter.

Rule: Let me in a request becomes requested + object + to let + pronoun + V1.

Memory hook: Enter becomes to let her enter.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Do not make noise."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher ordered them not to make noise.

Rule: Negative imperative uses not to.

Memory hook: The noise stops, and do not becomes not to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Never tell a lie."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He advised me never to tell a lie.

Rule: Never in commands is placed before to + verb.

Memory hook: Never tell becomes never to tell.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The officer said to the crowd, "Move back."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The officer ordered the crowd to move back.

Rule: Command changes to ordered + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Move back becomes to move back.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "What a beautiful painting!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She exclaimed with admiration that it was a very beautiful painting.

Rule: Exclamatory sentences change to exclaimed with emotion + that clause.

Memory hook: What a becomes very in indirect speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "How foolish I was!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He exclaimed with regret that he had been very foolish.

Rule: Exclamations of regret use exclaimed with regret and backshift.

Memory hook: How foolish becomes very foolish.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "Hurrah! We have won the match."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.

Rule: Hurrah becomes exclaimed with joy, and present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Hurrah is translated into joy.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Alas! I have lost my ring."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her ring.

Rule: Alas becomes exclaimed with sorrow, and have lost becomes had lost.

Memory hook: Alas is converted into sorrow.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Bravo! You have done well."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He applauded him, saying that he had done well.

Rule: Bravo expresses praise or applause.

Memory hook: Bravo becomes applauded.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Excellent! You have solved it."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher praised the student, saying that he had solved it.

Rule: Words of praise can become praised/applauded in indirect speech.

Memory hook: Excellent becomes praised.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Oh! I forgot the keys."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She exclaimed with surprise that she had forgotten the keys.

Rule: Oh may express surprise, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Oh becomes surprise.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What a terrible mistake!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He exclaimed with regret that it was a very terrible mistake.

Rule: What a becomes very, and exclamation becomes statement.

Memory hook: Exclamation marks disappear in indirect speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "How lucky we are!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: They exclaimed with joy that they were very lucky.

Rule: How + adjective becomes very + adjective.

Memory hook: How lucky becomes very lucky.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Would that I were rich!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She wished that she were rich.

Rule: Would that expresses a wish.

Memory hook: Would that becomes wished that.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "May you live long!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He blessed me that I might live long.

Rule: May used as blessing changes to blessed + object + that + might.

Memory hook: May in blessing becomes might.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to her son, "May you succeed!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She blessed her son that he might succeed.

Rule: Blessings with may change to blessed + object + that + might.

Memory hook: May you succeed becomes that he might succeed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to his enemy, "May you fail!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He cursed his enemy that he might fail.

Rule: May used negatively as curse changes to cursed + object + that + might.

Memory hook: Bad wishes become cursed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The priest said, "May God bless you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The priest prayed that God might bless me.

Rule: May in a prayer changes to prayed that + might.

Memory hook: Prayer keeps the meaning, not the exact word order.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Good morning, sir."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She respectfully wished him good morning.

Rule: Greetings change to wished/greeted, not a that-clause.

Memory hook: Good morning becomes wished good morning.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Good night."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He wished me good night.

Rule: Good night changes to wished + object + good night.

Memory hook: Greetings do not need tense backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said to the teacher, "Good evening, madam."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They respectfully wished the teacher good evening.

Rule: Greetings are reported with wished/greeted.

Memory hook: Good evening becomes wished good evening.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Farewell, my friends."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He bade farewell to his friends.

Rule: Farewell changes to bade farewell.

Memory hook: Farewell is reported as bade farewell.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Thank you, doctor."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She thanked the doctor.

Rule: Thank you changes to thanked + object.

Memory hook: Thank you becomes thanked.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Sorry, I am late."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He apologised to me for being late.

Rule: Sorry changes to apologised for + gerund/noun.

Memory hook: Sorry becomes apologised.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Yes, I did it."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She admitted that she had done it.

Rule: Yes in confession can become admitted, and did changes to had done.

Memory hook: Yes plus responsibility often becomes admitted.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "No, I did not steal it."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He denied that he had stolen it.

Rule: No plus accusation can become denied, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: No in defence often becomes denied.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The accused said, "I am innocent."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The accused claimed that he was innocent.

Rule: Claimed can replace said when the statement is a claim.

Memory hook: Legal statements often use claimed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The witness said, "I saw the accused near the gate."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The witness stated that he had seen the accused near the gate.

Rule: Stated is useful for formal reporting.

Memory hook: Witnesses state, friends usually say.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I promise I will return the money."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He promised that he would return the money.

Rule: Promise as reporting verb is followed by that clause.

Memory hook: I promise becomes he promised.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I swear I have told the truth."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She swore that she had told the truth.

Rule: Swear changes to swore, and present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: I swear becomes she swore.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I admit that I made a mistake."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He admitted that he had made a mistake.

Rule: Admit becomes admitted, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Made becomes had made after past reporting.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I deny that I copied the answer."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She denied that she had copied the answer.

Rule: Deny becomes denied, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Copied becomes had copied.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "You must not enter this room."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He warned me not to enter that room.

Rule: Must not in warning can become warned + object + not to + V1.

Memory hook: Must not enter becomes warned not to enter.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The doctor said, "Do not eat oily food."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The doctor advised him not to eat oily food.

Rule: Advice in negative imperative uses advised + object + not to.

Memory hook: Do not eat becomes not to eat.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: Mother said, "Brush your teeth before bed."
cards.definition:
Indirect: Mother advised the child to brush his teeth before bed.

Rule: Advice/order changes to advised/told + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Family grammar often becomes advised.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Please do not tell anyone."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He requested me not to tell anyone.

Rule: Polite negative request uses requested + object + not to.

Memory hook: Please do not becomes requested not to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Let the child answer."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher said that the child should be allowed to answer.

Rule: Let used as permission can become should be allowed to.

Memory hook: Let means allow in this case.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The judge said, "Let the accused speak."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The judge ordered that the accused should be allowed to speak.

Rule: Let in formal permission can be reported as ordered that should be allowed.

Memory hook: Courtroom let means permission.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I need not go there."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he need not go there.

Rule: Need not as modal may remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Need not often stays need not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I used to play badminton."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she used to play badminton.

Rule: Used to usually remains used to.

Memory hook: Past habit stays past habit.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I ought to help them."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he ought to help them.

Rule: Ought to generally remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Ought to stays ought to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I had better leave now."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had better leave then.

Rule: Had better usually remains had better, and now changes to then.

Memory hook: Had better stays, now changes.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I would like to meet you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he would like to meet me.

Rule: Would usually remains would, and pronouns change.

Memory hook: Would stays steady.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "You should not waste money."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She advised me not to waste money.

Rule: Should not as advice can become advised not to.

Memory hook: Advice can be reported more naturally with advised.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am going to buy a laptop."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was going to buy a laptop.

Rule: Am going to changes to was going to.

Memory hook: Going to becomes was going to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "They are going to open a shop."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that they were going to open a shop.

Rule: Are going to changes to were going to.

Memory hook: Planned future also backshifts.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have to finish this today."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had to finish that that day.

Rule: Have to changes to had to, this changes to that, today changes to that day.

Memory hook: Have to becomes had to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I do not have to attend the meeting."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she did not have to attend the meeting.

Rule: Do not have to changes to did not have to.

Memory hook: Obligation phrases also backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We are about to leave."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they were about to leave.

Rule: Are about to changes to were about to.

Memory hook: About to stays, are becomes were.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "The train is about to depart."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that the train was about to depart.

Rule: Is about to changes to was about to.

Memory hook: Even near-future expressions step back.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am unable to attend."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she was unable to attend.

Rule: Am unable changes to was unable.

Memory hook: Unable stays unable, am becomes was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I cannot understand this rule."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he could not understand that rule.

Rule: Cannot changes to could not, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Cannot becomes could not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I must finish the work before sunset."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had to finish the work before sunset.

Rule: Must showing obligation changes to had to.

Memory hook: Must becomes had to when it means necessity.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "You must not touch this wire."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He warned me not to touch that wire.

Rule: Must not as warning can become warned not to.

Memory hook: Dangerous instructions become warnings.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The sign said, "Do not park here."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The sign warned people not to park there.

Rule: Public instructions may be reported with warned/instructed + object + not to.

Memory hook: Here becomes there.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The notice said, "Submit the form by Monday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The notice instructed applicants to submit the form by Monday.

Rule: Official instructions use instructed + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Notices instruct, they do not politely chat.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The guide said, "Do not feed the animals."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The guide warned the visitors not to feed the animals.

Rule: Negative instruction uses warned + object + not to.

Memory hook: Zoo grammar protects fingers.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Can I borrow your pen?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether he could borrow my pen.

Rule: Can I changes to whether he could, and your becomes my.

Memory hook: Borrowed pens create both grammar and trust issues.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "May I come in?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked whether she might come in.

Rule: May I changes to whether she might.

Memory hook: Permission questions use asked whether.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to the teacher, "May I leave the class?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked the teacher whether he might leave the class.

Rule: May for permission changes to might in indirect speech.

Memory hook: May I leave becomes whether he might leave.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The student said, "Could you explain it again?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The student requested the teacher to explain it again.

Rule: Polite questions with could you may become requested + object + to.

Memory hook: Could you often hides a polite request.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Would you lend me your notes?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She requested me to lend her my notes.

Rule: Would you in a polite request can be reported as requested.

Memory hook: Would you lend becomes requested to lend.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What is your name?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me what my name was.

Rule: Wh-question uses statement order and pronoun change.

Memory hook: What is your name becomes what my name was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "How old are you?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked him how old he was.

Rule: Question word remains, but word order becomes statement order.

Memory hook: Are you becomes he was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Where is the nearest hospital?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me where the nearest hospital was.

Rule: Wh-question changes to statement order.

Memory hook: Where is becomes where was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The tourist said, "Which road leads to the fort?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The tourist asked which road led to the fort.

Rule: Present simple in question backshifts to past simple.

Memory hook: Leads becomes led.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The officer said, "Whose bag is this?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The officer asked whose bag that was.

Rule: This changes to that, and question order becomes statement order.

Memory hook: Whose bag is this becomes whose bag that was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Who wrote this answer?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked who had written that answer.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Wrote becomes had written.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Who is knocking at the door?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked who was knocking at the door.

Rule: Present continuous changes to past continuous.

Memory hook: Who is knocking becomes who was knocking.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What happened yesterday?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked what had happened the previous day.

Rule: Simple past changes to past perfect, and yesterday changes to the previous day.

Memory hook: Happened becomes had happened.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The coach said, "Why were you absent yesterday?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The coach asked him why he had been absent the previous day.

Rule: Past form of be changes to had been, and yesterday changes.

Memory hook: Were absent becomes had been absent.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "How much money do you need?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me how much money I needed.

Rule: Do question becomes statement order and present changes to past.

Memory hook: Do you need becomes I needed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "How many books have you read?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me how many books I had read.

Rule: Present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Have read becomes had read.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "What have you written?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked me what I had written.

Rule: Have written becomes had written.

Memory hook: The answer travels from have to had.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: My friend said, "Are you free tomorrow?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: My friend asked me whether I was free the next day.

Rule: Yes/no question uses whether/if, and tomorrow becomes next day.

Memory hook: Tomorrow becomes the next day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Will you be at home tonight?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I would be at home that night.

Rule: Will changes to would, and tonight becomes that night.

Memory hook: Tonight becomes that night.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Did you call me last night?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me whether I had called her the previous night.

Rule: Did changes to had + V3, and last night changes to previous night.

Memory hook: Did call becomes had called.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Do you remember this place?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I remembered that place.

Rule: Do question changes to statement order and this becomes that.

Memory hook: This place becomes that place.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Have you ever visited Jaipur?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me whether I had ever visited Jaipur.

Rule: Present perfect changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Have ever visited becomes had ever visited.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am sorry that I forgot your book."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He apologised for having forgotten my book.

Rule: Sorry can be reported as apologised for + gerund/perfect gerund.

Memory hook: Sorry becomes apologised for.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am grateful to you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She thanked me.

Rule: Expressions of gratitude can be reported with thanked.

Memory hook: Grateful words become thanked.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Congratulations! You have won the prize."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He congratulated me on winning the prize.

Rule: Congratulations becomes congratulated + object + on + gerund.

Memory hook: Congratulations on winning becomes congratulated on winning.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Welcome to our home."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She welcomed him to their home.

Rule: Welcome becomes welcomed + object.

Memory hook: Welcome is reported as welcomed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I object to your proposal."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He objected to my proposal.

Rule: Object can be used as reporting verb with to.

Memory hook: I object becomes he objected.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I agree with your plan."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She agreed with my plan.

Rule: Agree can replace said when meaning is agreement.

Memory hook: Agree remains direct and clean.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I refuse to sign the paper."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He refused to sign the paper.

Rule: Refuse is followed by to + V1.

Memory hook: I refuse becomes he refused.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I intend to start a business."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she intended to start a business.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Intend becomes intended.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I prefer tea to coffee."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he preferred tea to coffee.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Prefer becomes preferred.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I hate dishonesty."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she hated dishonesty.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Hate becomes hated, but the moral feeling remains.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I love solving puzzles."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he loved solving puzzles.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Love becomes loved in narration.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The scientist said, "This discovery will help patients."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The scientist said that that discovery would help patients.

Rule: This changes to that, and will changes to would.

Memory hook: Scientific statements backshift unless treated as timeless fact.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The manager said, "The office opens at ten."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The manager said that the office opened at ten.

Rule: Routine facts may backshift when reported as a statement by a person.

Memory hook: Opens becomes opened in ordinary reported speech.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The timetable says, "The train leaves at six."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The timetable says that the train leaves at six.

Rule: Present reporting verb says means no tense change.

Memory hook: Timetable says keeps the present tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am not going to accept this."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was not going to accept that.

Rule: Am going to changes to was going to, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: Not going to becomes was not going to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I have no money."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had no money.

Rule: Have as possession changes to had.

Memory hook: Have becomes had, sadly for the wallet too.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "My father works in a bank."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that his father worked in a bank.

Rule: My changes to his, and works changes to worked.

Memory hook: Family references follow the speaker.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "My mother is a doctor."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that her mother was a doctor.

Rule: My changes to her, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: Mother remains mother, grammar changes the pronoun.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "Our village has no hospital."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that their village had no hospital.

Rule: Our changes to their, and has changes to had.

Memory hook: Has becomes had.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Your answer is correct."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told me that my answer was correct.

Rule: Your changes to my, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: Your answer becomes my answer when spoken to me.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Your handwriting is beautiful."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told him that his handwriting was beautiful.

Rule: Your changes to his.

Memory hook: Praise follows the listener.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to them, "Your team played well."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told them that their team had played well.

Rule: Your changes to their, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Played becomes had played.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will meet you here tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would meet me there the next day.

Rule: Will becomes would, here becomes there, tomorrow becomes next day.

Memory hook: Three common shifts: will→would, here→there, tomorrow→next day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I saw this man here yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had seen that man there the previous day.

Rule: Saw changes to had seen, this to that, here to there, yesterday to previous day.

Memory hook: This-here-yesterday all move away from the direct quote.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "These flowers are fresh today."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that those flowers were fresh that day.

Rule: These changes to those, are to were, today to that day.

Memory hook: These becomes those.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am busy now but I will call later."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was busy then but he would call later.

Rule: Am changes to was, now to then, will to would.

Memory hook: Now and will both shift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The child said, "I broke the toy."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The child admitted that he had broken the toy.

Rule: Admitted can replace said when confessing.

Memory hook: A confession sounds better with admitted.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The boy said, "I did not break the window."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The boy denied that he had broken the window.

Rule: Denied is used when rejecting an accusation.

Memory hook: Did not break becomes had not broken.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I cannot come because I am ill."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she could not come because she was ill.

Rule: Cannot changes to could not, and am changes to was.

Memory hook: Cannot and am both backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I was absent because I was ill."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had been absent because he had been ill.

Rule: Past forms may change to past perfect for earlier reported events.

Memory hook: Was becomes had been in full backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "You have made the same mistake again."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher told me that I had made the same mistake again.

Rule: Have made changes to had made.

Memory hook: The same mistake follows students across tenses.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I had lost my ticket before I reached the station."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had lost her ticket before she reached the station.

Rule: Past perfect remains unchanged, while pronouns change.

Memory hook: Had lost stays had lost.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I will have finished the work by Monday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he would have finished the work by Monday.

Rule: Will have changes to would have.

Memory hook: Future perfect becomes conditional perfect.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will be waiting outside."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would be waiting outside.

Rule: Will be changes to would be.

Memory hook: Will be waiting becomes would be waiting.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We will have been working for ten hours."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they would have been working for ten hours.

Rule: Will have been changes to would have been.

Memory hook: Long tense, simple shift: will becomes would.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am to meet the officer."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was to meet the officer.

Rule: Am to changes to was to.

Memory hook: Formal future arrangement also backshifts.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "The show is about to begin."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that the show was about to begin.

Rule: Is about to changes to was about to.

Memory hook: About to survives, is becomes was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Let him try once more."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He suggested that he should be allowed to try once more.

Rule: Let him used for permission/suggestion can become should be allowed to.

Memory hook: Let him becomes allowed to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Let there be no delay."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She ordered that there should be no delay.

Rule: Let there be can become ordered/wished that there should be.

Memory hook: Formal let often becomes should be.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Mind your own business."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told me to mind my own business.

Rule: Command changes to told + object + to + V1.

Memory hook: Sharp commands become told to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Write your name at the top."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher instructed the students to write their names at the top.

Rule: Instructions use instructed + object + to.

Memory hook: Exam instructions become instructed.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The examiner said, "Do not write anything on the question paper."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The examiner instructed the candidates not to write anything on the question paper.

Rule: Negative instruction uses instructed + object + not to.

Memory hook: Do not write becomes not to write.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Kindly wait outside."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He requested me to wait outside.

Rule: Kindly indicates a polite request.

Memory hook: Kindly becomes requested.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to the shopkeeper, "Please give me fresh bread."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She requested the shopkeeper to give her fresh bread.

Rule: Please changes to requested.

Memory hook: Please give becomes requested to give.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "If I were rich, I would build a library."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that if he were rich, he would build a library.

Rule: Unreal conditional often remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Were and would already show unreality.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "If I had known this, I would have helped."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that if she had known that, she would have helped.

Rule: Third conditional usually remains largely unchanged, with this changing to that.

Memory hook: Had known and would have helped stay stable.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "If it rains, I will stay home."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that if it rained, he would stay home.

Rule: First conditional backshifts: rains to rained, will to would.

Memory hook: Real future condition becomes reported condition.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that unless I hurried, I would miss the bus.

Rule: Present in condition changes to past, will changes to would.

Memory hook: Hurry becomes hurried, will becomes would.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "When the bell rings, stop writing."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher instructed the students to stop writing when the bell rang.

Rule: Time clause present can backshift when reported.

Memory hook: Rings becomes rang.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "As soon as I reach home, I will call you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that as soon as he reached home, he would call me.

Rule: Present in time clause changes to past, will changes to would.

Memory hook: Reach becomes reached.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I wish I knew the answer."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she wished she knew the answer.

Rule: Wish sentence often keeps the unreal past form.

Memory hook: Knew stays knew because it already signals unreality.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I wish I had studied harder."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he wished he had studied harder.

Rule: Past regret with wish remains had + V3.

Memory hook: Had studied stays had studied.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "It is time we left."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that it was time they left.

Rule: It is time becomes it was time, but left remains as unreal past.

Memory hook: Is becomes was, left stays left.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I would rather you stayed here."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he would rather I stayed there.

Rule: Would rather structure usually remains, with pronoun/place changes.

Memory hook: Stayed stays stayed, here becomes there.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The principal said, "Students must wear uniforms."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The principal said that students had to wear uniforms.

Rule: Must for rule/obligation changes to had to.

Memory hook: School rules turn must into had to.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The sign says, "Visitors must wear helmets."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The sign says that visitors must wear helmets.

Rule: Present reporting verb says means no tense change.

Memory hook: Signs in present keep must.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I must be careful."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had to be careful.

Rule: Must for necessity changes to had to.

Memory hook: Must be careful becomes had to be careful.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "You need not worry."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told me that I need not worry.

Rule: Need not as modal may remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Need not is already modal-like.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I dare not speak."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he dare not speak.

Rule: Dare not as modal may remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Dare not stays dare not in formal grammar.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am used to waking early."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she was used to waking early.

Rule: Am used to changes to was used to.

Memory hook: Be used to backshifts only the be-verb.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I used to live in Bhopal."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he used to live in Bhopal.

Rule: Used to generally remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Used to is already past habit.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The boy said, "I am hungry."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The boy said that he was hungry.

Rule: Present simple changes to past simple.

Memory hook: Hunger survives narration.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The girl said, "I am thirsty."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The girl said that she was thirsty.

Rule: Am changes to was.

Memory hook: Am thirsty becomes was thirsty.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am afraid of dogs."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was afraid of dogs.

Rule: Present simple with adjective changes to past.

Memory hook: Fear changes tense, not species.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am proud of my result."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she was proud of her result.

Rule: My changes to her, and am changes to was.

Memory hook: Pride follows the speaker.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We are grateful to you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they were grateful to me.

Rule: We changes to they, you changes to me, are changes to were.

Memory hook: Gratitude changes pronouns carefully.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "My parents are coming tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that his parents were coming the next day.

Rule: Are coming changes to were coming, tomorrow to next day.

Memory hook: Tomorrow becomes next day.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I will not repeat this mistake."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she would not repeat that mistake.

Rule: Will not changes to would not, and this changes to that.

Memory hook: This mistake becomes that mistake, hopefully the last one.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have never lied to you."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had never lied to me.

Rule: Have never lied changes to had never lied, and you changes to me.

Memory hook: Never does not prevent backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The thief said, "I did not steal the watch."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The thief denied that he had stolen the watch.

Rule: Denial can be reported with denied, and simple past changes to past perfect.

Memory hook: Did not steal becomes had not stolen.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I cannot reveal the secret."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she could not reveal the secret.

Rule: Cannot changes to could not.

Memory hook: Secret remains secret, can becomes could.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I may be wrong."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he might be wrong.

Rule: May changes to might.

Memory hook: May weakens into might.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I must apologise."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had to apologise.

Rule: Must for obligation changes to had to.

Memory hook: Apologies also obey grammar.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We need more time."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they needed more time.

Rule: Need as main verb changes to needed.

Memory hook: Need becomes needed when it is a normal verb.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I do not understand the joke."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he did not understand the joke.

Rule: Do not changes to did not with base verb.

Memory hook: Do not becomes did not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I don't want any help."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she did not want any help.

Rule: Contracted don't expands and backshifts to did not.

Memory hook: Don't becomes did not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I didn't see the notice."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had not seen the notice.

Rule: Didn't see changes to had not seen.

Memory hook: Didn't see becomes had not seen.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I haven't completed the file."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had not completed the file.

Rule: Haven't completed changes to had not completed.

Memory hook: Haven't becomes had not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I won't sign the paper."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he would not sign the paper.

Rule: Won't changes to would not.

Memory hook: Won't becomes would not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I can't attend the class."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she could not attend the class.

Rule: Can't changes to could not.

Memory hook: Can't becomes could not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am reading now."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he was reading then.

Rule: Present continuous backshifts, now changes to then.

Memory hook: Now becomes then.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I was reading when you called."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had been reading when I had called.

Rule: Past continuous and simple past can backshift to past perfect forms.

Memory hook: Called becomes had called in full backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "We were sleeping when the storm started."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They said that they had been sleeping when the storm had started.

Rule: Past continuous and past simple may backshift in formal narration.

Memory hook: Storms disturb both sleep and tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I had locked the door before I left."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had locked the door before he left.

Rule: Past perfect usually remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Had locked stays had locked.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I have been ill for a week."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had been ill for a week.

Rule: Have been as state changes to had been.

Memory hook: Have been ill becomes had been ill.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have had this watch for ten years."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he had had that watch for ten years.

Rule: Present perfect of have becomes past perfect had had, and this becomes that.

Memory hook: Had had looks odd but can be correct.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I had had enough."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she had had enough.

Rule: Past perfect had had remains unchanged.

Memory hook: Had had may look strange, but grammar allows it.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "You are my best friend."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told me that I was his best friend.

Rule: You changes to I, my changes to his, and are changes to was.

Memory hook: Pronouns must be solved like a small logic puzzle.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "I will send you my notes."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told him that she would send him her notes.

Rule: I becomes she, you becomes him, my becomes her, will becomes would.

Memory hook: Notes travel through pronoun changes.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said to us, "We will meet you here tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They told us that they would meet us there the next day.

Rule: We to they, you to us, here to there, tomorrow to next day.

Memory hook: Four shifts in one sentence: pronoun, modal, place, time.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to her, "I gave you this book yesterday."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told her that he had given her that book the previous day.

Rule: Gave changes to had given, this to that, yesterday to previous day.

Memory hook: Gave becomes had given.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "I will return your pen tomorrow."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She told me that she would return my pen the next day.

Rule: Will to would, your to my, tomorrow to next day.

Memory hook: Returned pens are rare enough to remember.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said to them, "You must finish your work today."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He told them that they had to finish their work that day.

Rule: You/your change to they/their, must to had to, today to that day.

Memory hook: Must and today both shift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to us, "You should check your answers."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher advised us to check our answers.

Rule: Advice can be reported using advised + object + to.

Memory hook: Should check becomes advised to check.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The coach said to the players, "You can win if you work together."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The coach told the players that they could win if they worked together.

Rule: Can to could, present condition backshifts.

Memory hook: Team advice becomes they could.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Where there is a will, there is a way."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that where there is a will, there is a way.

Rule: Proverbs remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Proverbs are timeless, not time-shifted.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Practice makes perfect."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that practice makes perfect.

Rule: Universal/proverbial truths remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Practice makes perfect in every tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The sum of angles in a triangle is 180 degrees."
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher said that the sum of angles in a triangle is 180 degrees.

Rule: Mathematical facts remain unchanged.

Memory hook: Geometry does not backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I feel that the plan is risky."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he felt that the plan was risky.

Rule: Feel changes to felt, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: Opinion statements usually backshift.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I think he is honest."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she thought he was honest.

Rule: Think becomes thought, and is becomes was.

Memory hook: Think becomes thought.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I believe she can succeed."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he believed she could succeed.

Rule: Believe becomes believed, and can changes to could.

Memory hook: Belief backshifts too.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I hope you will come."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She said that she hoped I would come.

Rule: Hope changes to hoped, will to would, and you to I.

Memory hook: Hope becomes hoped.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I fear that I may fail."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He said that he feared that he might fail.

Rule: Fear changes to feared, and may changes to might.

Memory hook: May fail becomes might fail.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I wonder why he is late."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She wondered why he was late.

Rule: Wonder can be reporting verb, and is changes to was.

Memory hook: Wondered already reports the thought.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Do you really believe this story?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I really believed that story.

Rule: Yes/no question uses whether and statement order.

Memory hook: This story becomes that story.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Why don't you try again?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me why I did not try again.

Rule: Negative question changes to statement order.

Memory hook: Don't you becomes I did not.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Isn't this strange?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked whether that was strange.

Rule: Negative yes/no question becomes whether/if clause, this changes to that.

Memory hook: Isn't this becomes whether that was.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "Who can answer this?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: The teacher asked who could answer that.

Rule: Can changes to could, this changes to that.

Memory hook: Can answer becomes could answer.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "What should I do now?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked what she should do then.

Rule: Should remains should, now changes to then.

Memory hook: Should stays, now shifts.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Where should we sit?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked where they should sit.

Rule: Wh-question uses statement order, should remains.

Memory hook: We follows the speakers and becomes they.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "How could you forget my birthday?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked him how he could forget her birthday.

Rule: Could usually remains could, pronouns change.

Memory hook: Birthday questions are dangerous in every tense.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Would you like some tea?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked me whether I would like some tea.

Rule: Polite yes/no question can remain asked whether with would.

Memory hook: Would stays would.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Could I use your charger?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She asked me whether she could use my charger.

Rule: Could generally remains could, pronouns change.

Memory hook: Charger requests test both friendship and grammar.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Shall I open the window?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He asked whether he should open the window.

Rule: Shall I in offers/suggestions often changes to should.

Memory hook: Shall I becomes should he.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Shall we begin?"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She suggested that they should begin.

Rule: Shall we can express suggestion.

Memory hook: Shall we often becomes suggested.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What a mess this room is!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: He exclaimed with disgust that that room was a terrible mess.

Rule: Exclamatory sentence changes to exclaimed with emotion + that clause.

Memory hook: Exclamation becomes emotion plus statement.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "How sweet the mangoes are!"
cards.definition:
Indirect: She exclaimed with delight that the mangoes were very sweet.

Rule: How + adjective becomes very + adjective.

Memory hook: How sweet becomes very sweet.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Alas! The old tree has fallen."
cards.definition:
Indirect: He exclaimed with sorrow that the old tree had fallen.

Rule: Alas becomes sorrow, and has fallen becomes had fallen.

Memory hook: Alas is grief in one word.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: They said, "Hurrah! Our team has won."
cards.definition:
Indirect: They exclaimed with joy that their team had won.

Rule: Hurrah becomes exclaimed with joy.

Memory hook: Hurrah turns into joy.

cards.term: Change into indirect speech: She said, "Oh no! I have missed the train."
cards.definition:
Indirect: She exclaimed with regret that she had missed the train.

Rule: Oh no indicates regret or sorrow.

Memory hook: Missed trains create perfect narration examples.
